author: Mark Atwood
text:
## Eligibility evaluation: LICHEN vs grant-funder criteria (wqaa.10)

**Method note:** No deadlines are asserted anywhere below. The repo docs and sibling
beads name these specific programs: NLnet NGI0 Discovery, Shuttleworth Fellowship,
Mozilla OSS, EFF, Internet Society, ARDC, NSF (parent epic + wqaa.9). Other rows are
evaluated **by category only** and say so. Program-specific NOFO/deadline verification
is wqaa.9's job; this bead only maps LICHEN's facts to typical eligibility criteria.

### LICHEN facts used (with citations)

| Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Code GPL-3.0-or-later, docs CC-BY-4.0 | README.md "License"; AGENTS.md |
| Built on IETF standards (IPv6/RFC 8200, RPL/6550, SCHC/8724, CoAP/7252, OSCORE/8613, EDHOC/9528) | spec/01-architecture.md §1.1; README.md "Acknowledgments" |
| Mesh emergency/off-grid use case: SAR/CERT, disaster response, event comms, amateur radio | README.md "What It's For" (Tactical/Pro-Am, Hobby/Maker) |
| Runs on $30-class Meshtastic-compatible hobbyist hardware (T-Echo, RAK4631, Heltec) | README.md "Target Hardware"; AGENTS.md "Hardware Targets" |
| 500-node conference deployment deliverable at DEFCON/HOPE/CCC, $28.5k budget, resale cost recovery at $75/node | docs/prfaq-500node-deployment.md |
| Status: **Prototype** — Python sim complete; Rust + Zephyr "in progress"; no real-radio deployment yet | README.md "Project Status" |
| Solo project under personal GitHub (MarkAtwood/project-LICHEN); no legal entity, no 501c3, no fiscal sponsor anywhere in repo | repo structure; absence in all docs |
| Seattle, WA (US) base | PRFAQ dateline; procurement.md DHL route Shenzhen→Seattle |
| Budget figures are internally inconsistent: PRFAQ says $22.5k hardware @$45/unit landed; procurement.md binding quote says ~$9,988 total @~$20/unit | docs/prfaq-500node-deployment.md vs procurement.md |

### Criteria matrix (per funder category)

| Criterion | NLnet/NGI0 | Shuttleworth | Mozilla | EFF | ISOC | ARDC | NSF | Community broadband | Ham/emergency-comms funds | Univ. outreach | Conference sponsorship |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Open-source (GPL/CC) accepted | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | △ | ✓ | △ | ✗ | ✓ | △ | ✓ |
| No 501c3 / entity required (individual OK) | ✓ | ✓ | △ | n/a | △ | △ | ✗ | ✗ | △ | ✗ | ✓ |
| Geographic fit (US/Seattle) | ✓ (NL-based, global) | △ (SA/global) | △ | ✓ (US) | ✓ | ✓ (US) | ✓ (US) | local | ✓ | local | △ |
| Mission fit | ✓✓ (NGI: trust/decentralization) | ✓✓ (open knowledge) | ✓ | △ (advocacy, not grants) | ✓ (community networks) | ✓✓ (ham digital) | ✓ (research) | △ | ✓✓ | ✓ | ✓✓ |
| Milestone/reporting feasible solo | ✓ | ✓ | △ | n/a | △ | △ | ✗ | ✗ | △ | ✗ | ✓ |
| Deployable deliverable matches ($28.5k scale) | ✓ | △ (stipend, not line-items) | △ | n/a | △ | ✓ | ✗ (typ. ≫$28.5k) | ✗ | ✓ | △ | ✓ |
| Prototype-status risk (no field proof yet) | △ | △ | △ | n/a | △ | △ | ✗ | ✗ | △ | △ | ✓ |

✓ = typically satisfied by LICHEN as documented · △ = partial/conditional · ✗ = blocking gap · n/a = program type doesn't grant

### Per-category verdicts

**1. Open-source infrastructure funds — VERDICT: LIKELY (best fit).**
Named target: NLnet NGI0 Discovery (epic). Criteria mapping: funds individuals and
small teams without legal entity; OSI-license requirement met by GPL-3.0; NGI
privacy/trust/decentralization themes met by OSCORE/EDHOC + key-derived IPv6
(spec/06-security, spec/README). Caveats: (a) sibling wqaa.1's close note recorded
that as of 2026-07-25 NLnet's open calls were limited to specific topics
(Taler/Fediversity) — the general call must be rechecked before any application;
(b) NGI0 sub-funds differ on EU/associated-country eligibility — confirm which
sub-fund covers a US applicant. Sibling wqaa.2 (Shuttleworth): fellowship funds a
*person's* open work, which fits the solo-maintainer structure; the 500-node
deployment would be the fellow's project, not a line-item budget. Criteria-level fit
is strong; the open-knowledge/freedom framing requested in wqaa.2 is supported by the
all-public specs/vectors (CC-BY-4.0, test/vectors/).

**2. Amateur-radio & emergency-communications grants — VERDICT: LIKELY thematically, PARTIAL structurally.**
Named target: ARDC (epic). LICHEN explicitly scopes amateur-radio mesh experiments
and SAR/CERT/disaster-response use (README "What It's For"). $28.5k is a plausible
single-grant size for this category. Gap: ARDC is a US 501(c)(3) grantmaker; whether
it can fund an unincorporated individual directly or requires a fiscal sponsor /
organizational grantee must be verified (wqaa.9). Emergency-comms agencies and SAR
orgs fund *their own* equipment, so the realistic path is a partner org applying
with LICHEN as the deployed system — requires Mark to recruit a partner (SAR team,
CERT, ham club). No specific agency programs are named in the repo; evaluated by
category only.

**3. Digital-privacy / internet-freedom funders — VERDICT: PARTIAL.**
Named targets: Mozilla, EFF, Internet Society (epic). Mozilla: open-source criterion
met; but program intakes change and must be verified live — do not assume the MOSS-era
model still exists (evaluated at criteria level only). Internet Society: community-
networks theme is a genuine fit (mesh = community network infrastructure); grants
typically route through an organizational vehicle or chapter affiliation — individual
eligibility unverified. EFF: **Unlikely as a funder** — EFF is an advocacy/litigation
nonprofit, not a general grantmaker; realistic role is community visibility, not
money. Recommend dropping EFF from the funding target list (wqaa.9) unless its live
program list says otherwise.

**4. University / research outreach funds — VERDICT: UNLIKELY without an institutional partner.**
Named target: NSF (wqaa.9). NSF funds eligible US institutions (universities,
nonprofits); a solo unaffiliated individual cannot be the prime. The IETF-draft
pipeline (spec/drafts/, 5 drafts) and cross-implementation test vectors are real
research artifacts, so a subaward through a faculty collaborator is plausible — but
that is a human relationship Mark must establish. Everything else in this category
(outreach centers, labs) is evaluated by category only; none are named in the repo.

**5. Community broadband / digital inclusion programs — VERDICT: UNLIKELY.**
These typically require 501c3/municipal grantees and fund service delivery to a
population, not protocol R&D. LICHEN's emergency-comms framing is the only bridge,
and category 2 covers it better. Not pursued unless a specific program surfaces in
wqaa.9's research.

**6. Conference travel/deployment sponsorships — VERDICT: PARTIAL-to-LIKELY, cheapest path.**
Conferences named in the PRFAQ: DEFCON, HOPE, CCC. Village/community-side sponsorship
is in-kind or small-cash and does not require any legal entity — the only category
with zero structural gaps. Resale model ($75/node against $48 landed, PRFAQ) plus
sponsorship could cover a meaningful fraction of the $28.5k. NOTE the calendar: the
epic's plan ("submit before end of July for August DEFCON impact") has already lapsed
as of today (2026-08-28); the deployment target must be re-scoped to a future event
before any proposal names one.

**7. Federal research grants (NSF) — VERDICT: UNLIKELY as prime; possible as subaward.**
See category 4. $28.5k is far below typical federal award sizes; overhead, reporting,
and audit requirements make a direct application structurally impossible for the
current project form.

### Cross-cutting gaps (actions only a human can take)

1. **Choose a legal/financial vehicle.** No entity exists (personal GitHub repo, no
   501c3, no company, no fiscal sponsor in any doc). This is the single biggest
   eligibility blocker for categories 2, 3, 4, 5, 7. Options: fiscal sponsorship
   agreement, incorporate a nonprofit, or restrict applications to
   individual-eligible programs (NLnet, Shuttleworth).
2. **Verify live program status and deadlines** for the named funders (wqaa.9).
   Nothing in the repo records current NOFOs; the only recorded data point is the
   2026-07-25 note that NLnet's open calls were topic-limited (wqaa.1). Do not
   reuse the epic's July-deadline plan.
3. **Reconcile the budget.** PRFAQ ($28.5k total, $45/node landed) contradicts the
   binding DHL-backed quote in procurement.md (~$9,988 total, ~$20/node landed).
   wqaa.11 cannot produce a credible budget narrative until one figure is declared
   authoritative. A ~$10k hardware ask changes which funders are worth the effort.
4. **Decide how resale revenue is presented.** The $75/node cost-recovery model
   (PRFAQ) is earned income; some funders treat it as revenue/matching and will ask
   about it. A human should decide whether resale stays in the proposal.
5. **Recruit an organizational partner** (SAR/CERT team, ham radio club, university
   lab) to unlock categories 2 and 4 — relationships, not paperwork, are the gap.
6. **Set up a grant-capable bank/payment account** and a simple milestone-reporting
   practice (public quarterly reports in-repo would double as open-source evidence).

### Recommended priority from eligibility alone

1. NLnet/NGI0 (individual-eligible, best thematic fit) — after verifying the open call.
2. Shuttleworth (individual-eligible; reframe deployment as fellow's project).
3. Conference community sponsorship (no entity needed; re-scope event dates first).
4. ARDC (strong fit) — contingent on resolving gap #1 (entity/fiscal sponsor).
5. Defer: Mozilla, ISOC, NSF until gaps #1/#5 resolved; drop EFF as funder.

No funder names beyond those already in the epic/sibling beads were introduced; no
deadlines are claimed. Submission decisions rest with wqaa.13 and Mark.
